jamal_customer: Hi team — starting ~03:45 UTC we're seeing ~10% of requests to /v1/generate returning 429s for our production tenant. No code deploys on our side. Error sample: `HTTP/1.1 429 \n Retry-After: 30` . Can you confirm if we're hitting an RPM/TPM cap?

priya_support: sorry you're hitting this — we'll take a look. Can you paste a small curl example + any `X-RateLimit-*` headers you see? Also which region (us-east / eu-west)?

jamal_customer: us-east. curl:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-1","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -i```
Response headers (trimmed):```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 10 Mar 2026 03:46:12 GMT
Retry-After: 30
X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM: 6000
X-RateLimit-Remaining-RPM: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset-RPM: 1678521972```

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: ratecap-exceeded us-east (tenant=jamal_inc) — 427 events in 5m, heuristic spike detected

alex_sre: I can see a sustained mid-size spike from that tenant aligned to minute boundaries — looks like a bunch of ~60s long polling requests that refresh per-minute. Token bucket is draining.

kira_eng: can you confirm concurrency per API key? If they're doing long-lived streams and reauth per minute we can double-count tokens. Also check client retries: no backoff?

jamal_customer: our SDK opens one long poll per user every 50s (to get SSE updates). We did increase user syncs last night for an import job — maybe this overlapped with hourly billing tasks. No exponential backoff implemented.

priya_support: that combination explains it. Two suggested immediate mitigations: 1) tell client to add randomized jitter and exponential backoff on 429s, 2) reduce sync cadence (e.g., 1m -> 3m) while we investigate. We can also temporarily whitelist / raise quota if you need urgent throughput.

alex_sre: quick diagnostic to run (from your infra): capture a 5m trace of request timestamps (per-second) and count unique connections + `X-Forwarded-For`. If spike aligns exactly at :00 boundaries that indicates cron/minute-rollover folding. Example query:```SELECT date_trunc('second', ts) as s, count(*) FROM api_logs WHERE tenant='jamal_inc' AND ts > now()-interval '10 minutes' GROUP BY s ORDER BY s;```

kira_eng: on our side I'm checking the per-model serving pools — we have some capacity headroom but not enough to absorb a 2x sustained multiplier. If they want immediate relief we can flip them to a higher burst band for 1 hour (requires ops signoff).

jamal_customer: can you explain "minute-rollover folding"? We can't change the importer quickly.

priya_support: sure — when many clients poll on the same 60s cadence they create a spike every minute (requests bunch at the same second). Our rate limiter enforces RPM/TPM with per-second token refill. If a thousand clients simultaneously poll at :00 you see a large instantaneous rate causing Remaining-RPM to drop to 0 and 429s for the next requests. Spreading requests with jitter avoids that.

alex_sre: additional actionable items: - Instrument `X-Request-ID` on client side and compare with our logs. - Check for streaming connections not being reused (long TCP teardown can cause apparent new requests). - If they cannot alter cadence, we can schedule a short dedicated capacity bump (payment/approval) or temporary quota override.

priya_support: Jamal — do you want us to schedule a temporary quota bump while you roll out jitter? If so we'll need a written ok and expected duration. If not, try throttling to ~5r/s per API key as a mitigant and report back.

jamal_customer: OK let's do throttling client-side first (5r/s per key) and we'll implement jitter. Please prepare a one-hour quota increase as backup — I'll confirm after 15m. Thanks. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: If quota bump requested, create ticket `INC-302345` and tag @billing for approval.

priya_support: got it — marking this thread actionable. I'll follow up in 10m with any SRE findings.

alex_sre: FYI on the backend we also observed elevated token leakage from aborted connections with `Connection: keep-alive` — if their SDK is creating new TCP handshakes per poll that worsens the effective rate. Recommend keep-alive and pooling.

jamal_customer: thanks all. I'll push the client change now and report back in 12m.

priya_support: thanks — ping here when you've rolled the change and paste a short before/after count if possible. We'll keep the ops-bot alert muted while you test.
